censorship in China is pervasive, but also that it is not uniform, and that the social media landscape is complex and dynamic.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the censorship of political information in social media is pervasive and systematic, and that it is not limited to the deletion of messages containing sensitive keywords, but extends to the deletion of entire accounts.
the Chinese government actively monitors and deletes political messages on Sina Weibo and other Chinese social media.
the censorship in social media in China is pervasive, and the censorship is more severe in the western part of China.

social media in China are subject to active censorship, with a set of politically sensitive keywords triggering higher deletion rates.
the censorship of Chinese social media is not only a matter of blocking content, but also a matter of deleting it.
social media censorship in China is not a simple matter of blocking access to information, but also involves the active deletion of content that is already publicly available.
